$comment: The module notes, kept once (techsilon-oss KIT-STANDARD.md). /govkit-init shows them before the user says yes (skills/govkit-init/modules.mjs), the README module table is generated from them (tools/build-module-table.mjs), and every readMore guide carries the details. Module ids are the guardrail keys in govkit.json. default: "on" = installed unless skipped with a reason; "opt-in" = asked, off unless chosen.

modules.title: Project trackers
modules.youGet: A CLAUDE.md block with the branch flow and merge rules, a project hub for status, decisions and session handoffs, and a priority roadmap. Every other guardrail hangs off these.
modules.undo: Delete the govkit block in CLAUDE.md (between the govkit:start/end markers) and the two docs. govkit.json then has no trackers, which the doctor reports.

modules.title: Local release gate (CI fallback)
modules.youGet: Your CI checks, run on your machine with a PASS/FAIL scorecard, for when GitHub Actions can't run (minutes used up, an outage). With --pr it posts the evidence to the PR.
modules.changesOutsideRepo: With --pr only: one comment on the pull request.
modules.costs: Nothing to run; it needs tsx as a dev dependency (npm i -D tsx).
modules.undo: Set enabled:false with a reason in govkit.json, and delete scripts/release-gate.ts and release-gate.config.json.

modules.title: Your CI workflow
modules.youGet: A check that your repo has a CI workflow running the same checks as the release gate. govkit does not write it: a CI workflow is specific to your stack, and a wrong one is worse than none.
modules.changesOutsideRepo: Nothing from govkit. Your workflow uses GitHub Actions minutes.
modules.costs: Your CI's Actions minutes (free on public repos; 2,000 a month on the Free plan for private ones).
modules.undo: Set enabled:false with a reason in govkit.json.

modules.title: Block direct pushes to the release branch
modules.youGet: A git hook that refuses a push straight to the release branch, and prints the gh pr create command to use instead. On a private repo under GitHub's Free plan, it's the only enforcement there is.
modules.changesOutsideRepo: git config core.hooksPath in each clone (set by npm run prepare). Nothing on GitHub.
modules.undo: Set enabled:false with a reason in govkit.json, delete .githooks/, and run git config --unset core.hooksPath.

modules.title: Doc-sync check on pull requests
modules.youGet: On every PR, a check that code which changed came with its mapped doc. It warns on a PR to the working branch, and gates a PR to the release branch. You decide the pairs in scripts/source-doc-map.json.
modules.changesOutsideRepo: A GitHub Actions workflow, which posts or updates one comment on each PR.
modules.costs: About 10 seconds of Actions minutes per PR.
modules.undo: Set enabled:false with a reason in govkit.json, and delete the three files.

modules.title: Tracker freshness and ground truth
modules.youGet: At the start of a session, the facts from git and GitHub (branches, tags, CI, issues) next to what the trackers claim, and a warning when a tracker is older than the code. The plugin's session hook uses the same rule.
modules.changesOutsideRepo: Nothing. It reads git and, if available, gh.
modules.undo: Set enabled:false with a reason in govkit.json, and delete scripts/docs-sync-check.mjs. To silence only the session hook, set sessionHook:false.

modules.title: One version per release, tagged
modules.youGet: release:bump as the release PR's last commit, release:tag after the merge, and release:status to report a release with no tag or one shipped without a bump.
modules.changesOutsideRepo: release:tag pushes a v<version> tag to GitHub, when you run it.
modules.undo: Set enabled:false with a reason in govkit.json, delete scripts/release-version.mjs and its npm scripts. Existing tags stay.

modules.title: Supabase commands bound to this repo's account
modules.condition: Only offered when the repo uses Supabase (a supabase/ directory, or a SUPABASE_ variable in .env.example).
modules.youGet: npm run supabase runs the Supabase CLI with this repo's own token and refuses to run unless that token can see this repo's projects. A machine with several Supabase accounts can't apply a migration to the wrong one.
modules.changesOutsideRepo: Nothing beyond what your Supabase commands do. The token lives in your .env, which is not committed.
modules.undo: Set enabled:false with a reason in govkit.json, delete scripts/supabase.mjs and supabase/projects.json, and use the Supabase CLI directly.

modules.title: Track your work in GitHub Issues
modules.youGet: Your user stories, bugs and ideas kept as GitHub issues: standard labels (type, area, launch category, status), themed milestones, one pinned decision register for what only the owners can decide, and a closing format the session uses. A daily status report comes in 0.12.0.
modules.changesOutsideRepo: On GitHub: it creates the labels you are missing and one pinned issue (the decision register), each only after you say yes. It never changes or removes existing labels or pins.
modules.costs: Nothing for issue tracking. The daily report (0.12.0) uses about 1-2 GitHub Actions minutes a day; with no mail key it posts to a GitHub issue, with a mail-provider key it sends a designed HTML email.
modules.undo: Set enabled:false with a skippedReason in govkit.json. The labels and issues stay on GitHub; delete them there if you want.
